transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Well, I came in because I’m just tired all the time. I mean, I'm a teacher, so I know what it feels like to be tired at the end of the day, but this isn't that normal kind of tired. Even after a full night’s sleep, I just... I really have to push myself through everything. Just getting through grading, making dinner, and getting ready for the next morning takes so much effort.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly?
No, I don't think so. I live alone, so there's no one to really tell me if I do, but... I haven't ever woken myself up snoring or anything like that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yes, I think I have. I mean, most days I can still put on a smile for my students and get through the lessons okay. But underneath, it just feels like there’s this... gray, flat feeling. It kind of follows me home at the end of the day, and it makes the things I usually enjoy, like working in my garden or doing my watercolors, just seem really far away.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Well, not completely. Like I just mentioned with the gardening and my painting... I still care about them. I wouldn't say I've lost interest in the activities themselves. It's more just that I don't have the energy or the drive to actually get up and do them right now. But if I do force myself to start, I still enjoy it somewhat. So, no, the interest is still there, I think.
Have you been having trouble staying asleep at night?
No, I don't think so. Once I fall asleep, I usually stay asleep until my alarm goes off for school. I haven't really noticed waking up in the middle of the night.
How long have you been feeling this gray, flat mood?

It's been a while now. I'd say... probably about two years and two months. It really started right around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our whole household routine shifted then, and that's when I first noticed this feeling setting in.
During those two years, have you felt this gray, flat mood on most days?

Yeah, I would say most days. I mean, I can still smile for my students and get through the lessons fine, but... underneath, it just feels like there's this gray, flat feeling. It follows me home, and it just makes even my garden or my watercolors seem really far away.
During these past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your mood became much more severely depressed than usual?

No, I don't think so. It hasn't ever gotten severely worse or anything like that. It's just been this same, steady... flat feeling the whole time. Nothing really dips down into a severe depression, it just stays kind of gray.
Have you had low self-esteem?

Yeah, I do. I just keep thinking I should be handling everything better than I am. Like, when my lesson plans take twice as long to finish, or... or when I have to say no to mentoring a newer teacher at work, I just tell myself I’m letting my family and my school down. So, yes, I guess I have been pretty hard on myself lately.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I know I just said it takes me longer to finish my lesson plans, but it's not really because I can't focus. I can still pay attention to my students and get my grading done. My mind isn't wandering or anything like that... it just feels heavier to get through it all. So, no, my concentration is fine.
Have you been feeling hopeless?

Yes, I suppose I do. I don't feel like things are completely falling apart, exactly, but... I just have a really hard time believing this is going to get better. I don't see myself feeling lighter anytime soon, or getting back to being the person who used to actually look forward to going to museums or planning new projects or just enjoying a quiet afternoon. It just feels like this gray is how it's going to be.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
No, not really. My appetite has been pretty much the same as usual. I'm still eating my normal meals, and I haven't noticed any weight changes or anything. So, no changes there.
Have you been worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

No, I wouldn't say I'm worrying excessively. I mean, I have the normal stresses of teaching—worrying about a student who is struggling, or if a lesson will go well—but it's not like my mind is racing with anxiety about a million different things. It's more of that heavy, dull feeling I mentioned, rather than feeling anxious or worried all the time. So, no, not really.

Adjustment disorder remains a lesser possibility given onset around a life change, but duration/persistence favors F34.1.
